name: harness-connector-deepseek
description: Native VS Code client for DeepSeek Harness. Connect to your existing local Harness instance and continue the same workspaces and sessions directly inside VS Code.

walkthroughs.title: Get started with DeepSeek Harness
walkthroughs.description: Point VS Code at a Harness Host, then chat, approve, and review without leaving the editor.

steps.title: Open the panel
steps.description: The icon on the far left. It is already connecting on its own: in the default **auto** mode the extension reuses your local Harness credentials, and starts a Host when nothing is listening. [Open the panel](command:workbench.view.extension.deepseek-harness)

steps.title: Reach a connected status
steps.description: **Connected** in the status row means there is nothing left to do. If it says otherwise, press Connect; when the extension recognises a specific cause, the same row offers **Fix** and runs exactly that repair. [Connect](command:deepseekHarness.connect)

steps.title: Ask for something
steps.description: Type in the box at the bottom and press Enter. No setup step in between: the workspace and the session are created on your first send.

steps.title: Approve, then review
steps.description: Harness writes to your files directly and the extension never buffers them. Approvals are how you say go ahead; review cards are how you undo what happened.

deepseekHarness.host.markdownDescription: DeepSeek Harness host. Exactly three values are accepted — `127.0.0.1`, `localhost`, `::1`. Any other value is refused before a socket is opened, because the plugin only ever drives a Harness on the machine its extension host is running on. See *Remote development* in the README for what that means for Remote-SSH, WSL and containers.

deepseekHarness.port.markdownDescription: Port of the local `dsh web` instance. The default `dsh web` port is `3080`.

deepseekHarness.showSystemMessages.markdownDescription: Show plugin-injected system messages (e.g. `@deepseek-ai/dsh-system-prompt` runtime context, approval-policy notices). Hidden by default to reduce noise.

deepseekHarness.autoApproveApprovals.markdownDescription: Automatically answer tool-approval requests with `allow once` (only those answerable from VS Code). Equivalent of Copilot's `/autoApprove` — review the security trade-off before enabling.

enumDescriptions: Mint the cookie from `$DSH_HOME/.credentials.yaml` when that file is readable, and start `dsh web` when nothing is listening on the configured port. Works on a machine nobody prepared, and leaves an already-running Host exactly as it was.

Read the signing secret from `$DSH_HOME/.credentials.yaml` and mint the browser-session cookie locally, and nothing else. No paste and no extra process, but it means reading a file that also holds your model API keys — and it cannot work unless a Host is already running.

Start `dsh web` yourself and take the launch URL it prints. Nothing is read from disk and nothing is pasted — this extension starts a process for you, which is why it is opt-in. The command it runs is `deepseekHarness.launchCommand`, and the Host it started is stopped when the window closes.
Ask you for the launch URL printed by a `dsh web` you started. Nothing is read from disk and nothing is started. Run "DeepSeek Harness: Use Launch URL" to supply it.
deepseekHarness.sessionMode.markdownDescription:
How this extension obtains a Harness session.

- `auto` — mint if a credential is readable, and start a Host if nothing is listening (the default).
- `credentials` — mint the cookie locally from `$DSH_HOME/.credentials.yaml`, and nothing else. Requires a Host you started.
- `managed` — start `dsh web` and read the launch URL off its console. No credential file, no paste.
- `paste` — you start it and hand over the URL.

`auto` is the default from v0.2.8. Authentication and reachability are different problems: minting answers "who are you" and says nothing about whether anything is listening, so the old `credentials` default was a valid credential for a Host that did not exist. See the README's "How the session is obtained".

deepseekHarness.launchCommand.markdownDescription: The command `sessionMode: "managed"` runs to start a Host. The default binds an OS-assigned port, because managed launch reads the real port off the launch URL and pinning one only adds a way to fail. Whatever you put here runs through a shell, so wrappers and `npx` work. If the **default** command is not found (`dsh` is not on `PATH`), managed launch retries once with `npx -y @deepseek-ai/dsh@latest web --port 0` — on a remote connection that fetches `dsh` on the remote and starts the Host there. A command you set yourself is never substituted. Only read when a Host is started — changing it does not disturb a Host that is already running.

deepseekHarness.autoDiscover.markdownDescription: When the configured port answers nothing, look for a dsh Host elsewhere on loopback: ports pinned in `$DSH_HOME/profiles/<name>/cordis.patch.yml` first, then whatever is listening that answers the Host's own refusal text. Needed by the **desktop app**, which starts its Host on an OS-assigned port (`--port 0`) that changes every launch. The discovered port is used for this session only and is never written to your settings. Discovery always runs before managed launch, so an already-running Host is adopted rather than duplicated.

scripts.deploy: npm run build && vsce package --no-dependencies --out dist/harness-connector-deepseek.vsix && code --install-extension dist/harness-connector-deepseek.vsix --force
